question: Can strictly chronological low-complexity adaptive calibration improve later-period probability quality while preserving O0 ranking within each chronological evaluation window?

methods.raw_o0: chronologically trained StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000), no calibration
methods.expanding_platt: Platt calibration fitted only on outcomes observed before each evaluation window
methods.rolling366_platt: Platt calibration fitted only on the immediately preceding 366 observed outcomes
methods.block_platt: Platt calibration fitted only on the immediately preceding 104-row calibration block

interpretation.ranking_requirement: PASS within every chronological evaluation window for every tested monotonic Platt method
interpretation.probability_quality_requirement: NO clean pass: no adaptive method improves log loss, Brier, and ECE simultaneously over raw O0 in the rolling-origin aggregate
interpretation.future_holdout: Expanding Platt slightly improves log loss and ECE but worsens Brier; rolling-366 improves ECE but worsens log loss and Brier
interpretation.decision: Do not promote an adaptive-calibration candidate as a production model and do not create O14 from this diagnostic alone
interpretation.next_question: The remaining weakness is more consistent with discrimination/feature relationship drift than with a standalone calibration problem. Preserve O0 and investigate feature-level temporal relationship stability rather than adding another calibration heuristic.
